meta.method: pdftocairo -svg vector path extraction (fills, stroke colours, path geometry) plus pdftotext -bbox-layout for text, validated against pdftoppm PNG renders
meta.confidence: high for nodes, labels, shapes, colours and edges (all derived from the vector content stream, with every arrowhead accounted for). Medium for column and faction naming, and for novella versus short story, where the two shapes are identical.

shortStory.shape: rounded rectangle with a chamfered/cut top-left corner, plus a "(Book N)" label line

novella.shape: rounded rectangle with a chamfered/cut top-left corner. GEOMETRICALLY IDENTICAL to Short Story, distinguished only by the absence of a "(Book N)" label

exclusiveUnnumberedShortStory.shape: sharp-cornered rectangle with a folded top-right corner

notes: "(Book N)" on a node means the story is contained in numbered anthology N.
"(eBook)" marks an eBook-only release. It is an annotation, not a shape.
"(Anthology)" marks a node that is itself an anthology container.
The legend contains no plain sharp-cornered rectangle other than the Exclusive Unnumbered Short Story swatch.

renderVerified: Malcador: First Lord of the Imperium (circle, audio drama)
meta.renderVerifiedNote: These two nodes are filled with a gradient and carry no companion stroke path, so only the fill bounding box survives in the vector stream. Their shape was read from a 250 dpi render instead of from path geometry.
caveats: Node fill colour is the reliable faction signal. Vertical lanes are reused as the timeline descends, so column xRange is the observed extent of that colour and not a hard boundary.
Novella and short story are the same shape. Nodes with format "novella" are inferred from the absence of a "(Book N)" label and are marked confidence "medium".
Column and faction names are inferred from the shoulder-pad artwork and from the books in each lane. The chart never writes a legion name.
bookRef is always null. The chart prints anthology references only, never main-series numbers.
Labels preserve the chart text verbatim, including its typographical errors (for example "Tallarn: SIren", "Herald of Sangiunius", "The Devine Adoratrice", "Vulcan Lives").
